title: Quicklaunch SDK minikits: Next.js, FastAPI, Go HTTP & CLI examples
creator: Miguel Ortega
description: Create a set of compact, opinionated starter kits that demonstrate Redwood SDK best-practices across three languages and runtimes: TypeScript (Next.js), Python (FastAPI), Go (simple HTTP server) plus a minimal cross-platform CLI. Each kit should be copy-paste friendly, ~100-300 lines total, and highlight: streaming ergonomics (resumable/partial responses, backpressure), idempotent retry patterns with jitter and token-cost-aware retries, structured output parsing, auth via env/KV, simple local dev + Dockerfile, and one integration test. The goal is to reduce first-time integration time for engineers, provide clear patterns for retries/streaming, and serve as canonical snippets for docs and quickstarts. Deliverables include repos/examples, README cookbooks, short demo recordings, and a single combined reference PR that links to SDK APIs and docs.
acceptance_criteria: Next.js example demonstrates server-side and client-side streaming with resumable reconnect and token-level progress UI
FastAPI example shows streaming endpoints, clean Python async patterns, retry wrapper for transient 429/5xx with exponential backoff and idempotency key guidance
Go example provides a minimal net/http server demonstrating streaming response handling, graceful shutdown, and KV-cache usage pattern
CLI example (TypeScript/Go) shows a resumable upload + streaming inference flow with clear retry/backoff and exit codes
All examples include a README with setup, env vars, Dockerfile, and 1 integration test runnable in CI
Code samples use the unified Redwood SDK surface (matching current public API) with examples for streaming, function calls, and embeddings where relevant
Each example is <= 300 lines (excluding vendor/SDK code) and has a short demo GIF or 60s screen recording linked
Cross-language patterns section in README summarizing retry parameters, suggested defaults, and caveats for production deployments
tasks: Draft canonical patterns doc (cookbook-snippets.md) with examples of backoff, jitter, idempotency, and streaming resumption
Implement Next.js starter: serverless edge-compatible page + client streaming UI
Implement FastAPI starter: async streaming endpoint + retry wrapper utility
Implement Go starter: small HTTP server with streaming client and graceful shutdown
Build CLI example: ts-node (or compiled Go) tool showing resumable prompt + append semantics
Create Dockerfiles and minimal CI integration tests for each kit
Write README and cross-language comparison section
Record 60s demo for each starter and attach GIFs
Open combined PR linking to SDK docs and update quickstart landing page
